raw_response:
I've been working this land since I was twenty years old. I don't need a book to tell me what to do — I learned from my father, and from every season of drought, flood, and good harvest since then. I'm alone now, so I keep things simple. Six mu is manageable. I know my well, I know my soil, I know when the rains come and when they don't.

**My wheat plan (October through next June):**
All six mu go to wheat in the autumn. I'll plough the field first — I always plough, it breaks up the hardpan from summer maize. I buy improved seed from the village shop, the same variety I've used for several years now. It performs well here. I apply compound fertilizer as a base when I plant, then top-dress with urea at jointing in spring. I'll irrigate three times: once before the ground freezes (冬灌), once at jointing, once at heading. Two pesticide sprays — one herbicide in late autumn, one fungicide if the powdery mildew shows up in spring like it usually does. I expect around 450 jin per mu, maybe a bit more if spring rains cooperate.

**My maize plan (June through September/October):**
The day after I harvest wheat, I get the maize in the ground. No time to waste — the season is short. I use hybrid seed, always. Everyone switched years ago and the yields prove it. I do rotary tillage to chop up the wheat straw and mix it in — no sense burning it, it feeds the soil. Base fertilizer goes in with planting, then I side-dress at the big bell stage (大喇叭口期) when the plant is really pushing. Irrigation twice — once right after planting if it's dry, once at silking. I spray herbicide early and watch for stem borers. Usually one more pesticide application is enough. I expect 550 jin per mu on a decent year.
